title: Derived PartialEq/Eq on EmailAddress is byte-exact; RFC 5321 §2.4 domain part is case-insensitive
description:
header_typed.rs:40-46 derives `PartialEq, Eq` on EmailAddress. The derive compares `name` and `address` as byte-exact `Option<String>` values.

For the `address` field — an RFC 5322 addr-spec — RFC 5321 §2.4 specifies the *domain* portion as case-insensitive. `JAMES@example.com` and `james@example.com` refer to the same mailbox at the SMTP/RFC level. Most JMAP server code that compares addresses needs case-folding on the domain.

Caller-facing consequence: a caller using EmailAddress as a HashMap key (once Hash is derived — currently absent), as a HashSet member, or with `==` will get two-or-more representations of the same address as distinct entries:

    EmailAddress { name: None, address: Some("james@example.com".into()) } !=
    EmailAddress { name: None, address: Some("james@EXAMPLE.COM".into()) }

This is silent. The derive looks innocuous; the bug surfaces only when a caller compares parsed addresses from different sources.

This is structurally similar to MIME-o2c.24 (HeaderDateTime instant-vs-field equality) but for EmailAddress's domain folding. Filing separately because the fix differs: HeaderDateTime needs offset normalisation, EmailAddress needs domain-case-fold on the address portion (and possibly on display-name unicode normalisation, though that is fuzzier).

Fix options:
- Document that PartialEq is byte-exact on `address` and direct callers to `address_eq()` / `domain_eq()` helpers (not currently provided).
- Provide `EmailAddress::canonical_address(&self) -> Option<String>` that lowercases the domain part, and document the canonical form.
- Drop the derive and write a hand-rolled PartialEq.

This is opinion-leaning because the derive is "standard Rust practice" but the contract gap is real. Marking P3 — would-prefer-fixed but not block-merge.

Line refs:
- header_typed.rs:40 `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]`
- header_typed.rs:44-45 `address: Option<String>` — the field whose comparison semantics differ from RFC 5321.
close_reason: Documentation batch on the typed header surface: (.7) parse_header_typed now states trailing CRLF is permitted-but-not-required (matching the implementation); (.8) EmailAddress.name and AddressGroup.name field docs now state the trim+empty-to-None normalization; (.12) HeaderValueTyped doc has a Serde Wire Format section pinning the current externally-tagged shape and explicitly distinguishing it from RFC 8621 wire format (callers responsible for that mapping); (.17) parse_header_typed doc now carries one runnable example per HeaderForm variant (six total); (.24) HeaderDateTime has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is field-wise not instant-wise, with a worked example and the to_timestamp escape hatch; (.25) EmailAddress has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is byte-exact (no RFC 5321 domain case-folding) and pointing callers at manual canonicalisation; (.30) parse_header_typed doc has an Empty-Result Ambiguity table making explicit that callers cannot distinguish malformed-vs-empty-vs-non-UTF-8 and flagging the future-direction (strict variant / warnings tuple). No code changes.
